map.肾病/低白蛋白影响: Effect of kidney disease / low albumin
map.GA是HbA1c的重要补充。① 评估短期血糖控制（如药物调整后2-3周疗效）；②: GA is an important complement to HbA1c: (1) assessing short-term glycaemic control, such as the response 2-3 weeks after a medication change; (2) gestational diabetes management, where red cell lifespan change makes HbA1c unreliable; (3) haemodialysis patients, where HbA1c cannot be trusted; (4) perioperative glycaemic management; (5) patients with iron deficiency or haemolytic anaemia.
map.低白蛋白血症（<35g/L）、肾病综合征、甲状腺功能异常、肝硬化等会影响GA准确: Hypoalbuminaemia (under 35g/L), nephrotic syndrome, abnormal thyroid function and cirrhosis all affect GA accuracy. Reference ranges for older adults and children differ slightly. Reading GA together with HbA1c gives a fuller picture of glycaemic control.

map.糖化白蛋白 4.2 mg/dL、白蛋白 4.0 g/dL：GA(%)=糖化白蛋白: Glycated albumin 4.2 mg/dL with albumin 4.0 g/dL: GA(%)=glycated albumin/albumin×17.1≈18% (some laboratories use the GA/albumin ratio AGR). The normal GA reference is about 11%-16%, and a raised value indicates glucose has been high over the past 2-4 weeks.
map.GA 与 HbA1c 有什么区别？: How does GA differ from HbA1c?
map.HbA1c 反映约 2–3 个月平均血糖，GA 反映约 2–4 周，时间窗更短，: HbA1c reflects about 2-3 months of mean glucose while GA reflects about 2-4 weeks, a shorter window that is more sensitive to recent change.
map.严重肾病、肝病、甲状腺功能异常及大剂量白蛋白输注可影响白蛋白水平，使 GA 解读: Severe kidney disease, liver disease, abnormal thyroid function and large albumin infusions all shift albumin levels and skew GA interpretation.
